claims: As of early April 2026, Crunchyroll is facing a new class action lawsuit filed in March 2026 for alleged violations of the Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA).
As of early April 2026, Crunchyroll is facing a second lawsuit related to a major data breach.
Crunchyroll reached a $16 million settlement in 2023 regarding privacy concerns.
The class action lawsuit Cabonios v. Crunchyroll, LLC was filed in California federal court.

The lawsuit Cabonios v. Crunchyroll, LLC accuses Crunchyroll of sharing users' email addresses, device IDs, and specific anime titles watched with third-party marketing firms like Braze without consent.
The lawsuit Cabonios v. Crunchyroll, LLC alleges violations of the Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA).
The Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) is a federal law designed to protect user viewing records.
Plaintiffs in the Cabonios v. Crunchyroll, LLC lawsuit are seeking statutory damages of $2,500 per violation.
The 2023 settlement followed similar privacy concerns over user data sharing with Facebook.
Reports indicate a security incident occurred around March 12, 2026.
A third-party vendor named Telus Digital was breached.
The breach potentially exposed 100GB of user data including emails and IP addresses.
The breach potentially exposed payment details.
A second class action lawsuit was filed accusing Crunchyroll of negligence in data security.
The second class action lawsuit accuses Crunchyroll of failing to properly encrypt information.
The second class action lawsuit accuses Crunchyroll of not notifying users in a timely manner.
Crunchyroll has confirmed they are aware of the claims.
Crunchyroll is investigating with cybersecurity experts.
In September 2023, Crunchyroll settled a VPPA lawsuit for $16 million.
The September 2023 settlement regarded the use of the Facebook Pixel tool.
The Facebook Pixel tool tracked user viewing history without permission.
Eligible users in the 2023 case received approximately $30.
